objective: Close the re-audit's actionable defects, explicitly reverify the unresolved prior findings and prove the exact private Classic/RF app/mod pair through safe installed and real-source acceptance.
scopeNote: The 29 actionable findings include 24 carried-forward findings and five new findings. Eleven other prior findings remain not reverified. These are not 29 demonstrated exploits or 40 newly reproduced defects.
nonNegotiables: Public Classic 4.2.1/mod 3.4.0.7 and its release/update story remain unchanged.
Existing Classic 4.2.2/mod 3.4.0.8 and RF 5.0.1/mod 5.0.0.1 artifacts remain immutable private evidence; future version/build decisions require approval.
Reproduce against current production code before editing. If already fixed in workspace, add closure proof and skip unnecessary rewrite.
Use actual production imports and actual Preact lifecycle tests. Frozen exit-0 diagnostics and copied algorithms are not regression proof.
No installer, uninstall, game/mod switch, real credential change, active-save mutation or public publication is authorized by creating this plan.
Destructive/fault tests use disposable profiles and copied saves; the user's active Save 1 is not a scratch fixture.

effort.meaning: Planning allowances if the described work remains necessary, not a quote or measured schedule. Includes package-level engineering/test effort, excludes external waiting, certificate procurement and unpredictable hosting/game availability.

coverage.title: Mod export success still does not prove bytes were written
coverage.state: Confirmed in the newly packaged RF mod source; no game fault injection
coverage.detail: The copy wrapper discards copyFile's result and accepts a nonthrowing call plus an existing destination. Move recovery can then delete the source. Atomic/direct/mirror write paths do not consistently check write and close outcomes; saveFile fallback equates pcall success with persisted success.
coverage.impact: Disk, permission or nonthrowing I/O failures can leave stale or damaged exports while success bookkeeping advances. This finding concerns the packaged code; it does not claim the current save has been damaged.

coverage.title: Opaque browser origins still inherit native loopback trust
coverage.state: Reproduced in isolated candidate-code fixtures
coverage.detail: `getRequestOrigin` turns explicit Origin: null and malformed origins into an empty string. Both the write guard and WebSocket origin guard then take the no-origin local-client branch. The fixture accepted both, while rejecting an ordinary hostile HTTPS origin.
coverage.impact: A browser-origin boundary can be bypassed on locally reachable privileged HTTP/WS paths. This is a boundary reproduction, not a live browser exploit against your machine.

coverage.title: FTP detail filenames can escape the intended cache
coverage.state: Reproduced in an isolated Windows-path fixture
coverage.detail: `syncFtpDetailsCache` only checks that a remote entry starts with animals_ and ends with .json. Backslashes and traversal components survive into path.join. A mocked listing directed the download to C:\audit\outside.json instead of the userData subtree.
coverage.impact: A malicious or compromised configured FTP source can influence a local write destination outside the cache. No real files were created or overwritten by the fixture.

coverage.title: Failed FTP replacement deletes the last good cache first
coverage.state: Reproduced in an isolated filesystem fixture
coverage.detail: `safeDownload` unlinks localFinal before attempting rename. With a simulated EACCES at rename, it returned false with the final file absent and only the temporary file remaining. Per-pen FTP replacement contains the same unlink-before-rename sequence.
coverage.impact: A transient replacement failure removes the last usable local snapshot and degrades offline/recovery behavior. This is local cache loss, not demonstrated game-save corruption.

coverage.title: Sampled animal count correction still changes averages
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation
coverage.detail: Sampled buckets scale count and weighted sums together, then correct count alone to meet the reported population. Later averages divide unchanged sums by corrected counts. The inspected average helper also drops nonpositive sums, so measured all-zero health does not become an explicit aggregate zero.
coverage.impact: Herd average health, weight, age and genetics can change solely because head counts were reconciled; unknown and measured zero remain conflated at the aggregate boundary.

coverage.title: Courseplay finance still falls back to purchase price
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation
coverage.detail: The incremental-fleet finance branch reads row.sellValue, row.sellPrice or row.price. The inspected vehicle serializer writes purchase price into row.price and the shown sell-value path stores it under ads.sellValue.
coverage.impact: Vehicle asset value and net worth can be inflated on this collection path.

coverage.title: Courseplay compatibility still traverses the fleet twice per update
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation; no FPS benchmark
coverage.detail: FarmDashboard:update calls the compatibility tick. When Courseplay is loaded, shieldFleetIfNeeded performs two complete fleet passes on each tick, without the no-Courseplay pending-work gate.
coverage.impact: Steady-state frame work grows with fleet size even when no shop/vehicle transition needs repair. The audit did not measure an FPS loss.

coverage.title: Adaptive cadence still uses a requested interval that setters do not update
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation
coverage.detail: _userCollectionCycleMs is captured during config load and preferred by adaptive cadence. The inspected synced-settings and setInt paths update config.collectionCycleMs but not that requested-value field.
coverage.impact: The user's interval choice can be overwritten or ignored by the next adaptive adjustment.

coverage.title: Collector failure still collapses into an empty payload
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation; full scheduler fault injection outstanding
coverage.detail: `safeCollect` returns an empty table both for missing/failed collection and for empty results, without an error status. Legacy collection consumes that result, and other completion paths still update cached data/finish slices without a uniform failure envelope.
coverage.impact: Downstream code cannot reliably distinguish a successful empty section from a failed collection; stale/clear/freshness decisions remain fragile.

coverage.title: Station-name rules still fabricate sell offers
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation
coverage.detail: Although synthetic whole stations were removed, Method 8 still inserts products and fixed multipliers into existing named stations, including Grain Mill and Biogas Plant. Those prices feed the crop min/max/best-location calculation.
coverage.impact: The dashboard can recommend an offer that was inferred from a station name rather than observed from the game.

coverage.title: Bale enumeration still budgets accepted rows rather than examined entries
coverage.state: Packaged-mod source confirmation
coverage.detail: The iterator restarts pairs over a source table, skips previously seen entries, and increments its cap primarily for newly accepted entries. A large table of non-bale or already-seen objects can therefore require a broad scan in one slice.
coverage.impact: The nominal row budget does not bound actual work and can still cause long game-thread slices.

coverage.title: FTP intervals can overlap and stale downloads can still commit files
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation of the overlapping FTP branch
coverage.detail: The interval starts another batch without awaiting the previous batch. Poll generation checks occur before safeDownload and after it, but safeDownload replaces the final file internally before the post-download generation check. Generation-specific temporary names do not prevent an older operation from committing the shared final file.
coverage.impact: Slow connections or configuration changes can create duplicate work and replace current disk data with an obsolete operation, even if renderer ingestion is later skipped.

coverage.title: The HTTP total deadline still behaves as an idle timeout
coverage.state: Reproduced with candidate code and a simulated trickle response
coverage.detail: The 45-second deadline is checked when entering a request/redirect, but there is no independent wall-clock cancellation timer for an active body. A mocked stream was still pending at 60 seconds and then returned HTTP 200. Response aborted/error settlement also remains incomplete in the inspected function.
coverage.impact: A slowly streaming or prematurely aborted feed can keep collection work pending beyond the advertised deadline and amplify polling overlap.

coverage.title: FTP pen freshness still trusts client mtime and a missing dirty index
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation
coverage.detail: Bulk detail sync compares remote mtime with the downloaded file's local mtime. Per-pen detail re-fetches only when dirtyAt is positive and newer than the local timestamp; a cached file with a missing index can therefore be reused indefinitely.
coverage.impact: Clock skew and missing/stale indexes can leave animal detail old even while the overview continues updating.

coverage.title: Unstamped export freshness is still renewed after restart
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation of the accepted unstamped-export path
coverage.detail: The content hash excludes weather and is not included in the persisted cache identity. On new in-memory state, the same unstamped export receives a new receipt-based lastLuaReceivedAt.
coverage.impact: Old cached data can appear fresh after a restart; an unstamped weather-only update can also be missed by freshness detection. This is a legacy/unstamped-input path, not a claim that every current export lacks a timestamp.

coverage.title: Hold and snapshot logic still retains legitimately cleared sections
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation
coverage.detail: Backup updates remember nonempty animals without clearing the prior backup on an authoritative empty result. Snapshot forwarding restores previous animals/stock when the next section is empty; stock and RF hold branches still conflate empty with unavailable.
coverage.impact: Removed animals, exhausted stock or disabled optional data can reappear during fallback/restart, undermining confidence in the dashboard.

coverage.title: Detail generations are still dropped and zero pens can receive old animals
coverage.state: Reproduced in isolated candidate-helper fixtures
coverage.detail: `makeCacheEntry` still drops generatedAt. A husbandry reporting zero animals accepted two retained detail rows and was marked hydrated. The newer code prefers some smaller unique-ID lists, but does not establish generation correctness or a zero-population tombstone.
coverage.impact: Sold or removed animals can reappear as detail rows, and choosing the newest complete pen snapshot remains unreliable.

coverage.title: Ambiguous fleet ownership is still promoted from farm heuristics
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation
coverage.detail: The transient-pool resolver scores farms using livestock, land, current fleet and ADS presence, then writes the selected farm into ownerFarmId/farmId when the fallback applies.
coverage.impact: An ambiguous ownership guess can become authoritative-looking fleet and financial data on the wrong farm.

coverage.title: One XML vehicle can still be consumed through two matching indices
coverage.state: Reproduced using the candidate matching branches
coverage.detail: A configuration-key match removes a row from one list but leaves its UID index available. The fixture matched the same XML object first by configuration and then again by UID.
coverage.impact: Distinct live vehicles can inherit the same saved identity, ownership or values, producing duplicate or misleading fleet information.

coverage.title: Field IDs and farmland IDs still share a collision-prone seen set
coverage.state: Candidate-source confirmation of one remaining branch
coverage.detail: The Lua-only append branch checks seenKeys against both field.id and farmlandId even though XML keys use farmlandId-or-id. A valid field can be suppressed because its field ID happens to equal a different record's farmland ID. The separate prior ownership-precedence branch was not fully re-executed here.
coverage.impact: Valid fields may disappear from merged output when identifier domains collide.

coverage.title: XML change detection still misses changes below the maximum mtime

coverage.detail: The fingerprint remains maximum mtime plus total size. Changing one file's mtime from 1000 to 2000 while another remained 9999 produced the same fingerprint, 9999:200.
coverage.impact: A valid XML update can be skipped and old field/vehicle/economy data retained until another fingerprint component changes.

coverage.state: Reproduced in configuration fixtures; retained poller object confirmed in candidate source

decisions.title: Private version and build identity
decisions.recommended: Keep public Classic 4.2.1/mod 3.4.0.7 unchanged. Build into a fresh private directory with a unique external build ID and hashes; obtain explicit approval before any visible version change.
decisions.tradeoff: Reusing a private visible version is possible only with unmistakable immutable identity; overwriting a previously distributed binary is not acceptable.

decisions.title: Privileged native, LAN and proxy authorization
decisions.due: During RP-02, before RP-03 policy implementation
decisions.recommended: Reject opaque/malformed browser origins and require explicit authorized capability for privileged operations. Support only documented direct/local/proxy paths; unconfigured proxy trust is disabled.
decisions.tradeoff: Some legacy no-Origin native clients may need a deliberate migration path. Do not preserve compatibility by restoring unauthenticated loopback privilege.

decisions.title: Shared game-target writer ownership
decisions.due: During RP-02; enforce before RP-16 acceptance
decisions.recommended: Allow multiple readers but one authorized writer per actual target. Use tested local coordination; dedicated multi-host edits require server coordination or an explicit single-writer/read-only support policy.
decisions.tradeoff: Read-only secondary instances are safer but need clear UX. A peer-port probe or local mutex cannot guarantee remote distributed exclusivity.

decisions.title: Source identity, generation and legacy compatibility
decisions.recommended: Use available durable context identity plus source epoch/revision, separate clock domains and explicit section outcomes. Legacy missing metadata remains lower-confidence with bounded refresh.
decisions.tradeoff: Additive schema and cache migration work is larger than a local timestamp patch, but avoids incompatible fixes across mod, disk and frontend.

decisions.title: Windows and FS25 safe-write capabilities
decisions.recommended: Use only documented/tested platform operations; preserve last-good bytes and report failure whenever commit cannot be established.
decisions.tradeoff: A recoverable multi-step protocol may require backup/journal handling. Do not claim all-files atomicity or assume return values from pcall alone.

decisions.title: Frontend lifecycle test environment
decisions.recommended: Reuse the existing compatible test stack with actual Preact DOM/effect execution and production TypeScript imports. Add a pinned compatible runner only if required.
decisions.tradeoff: A new runner adds maintenance; copied functions and simulated hooks are cheaper but cannot close the actual production lifecycle defects.

decisions.title: Performance and UX acceptance budgets
decisions.recommended: Ratify hardware, save sizes, transfer limits, p95/p99 slice and interaction budgets before judging results; retain the existing 45-second total HTTP deadline if still the product requirement.
decisions.tradeoff: Targets are proposed, not measured achievements. Avoid an unsupported universal FPS or accessibility certification claim.

decisions.title: Signing and private distribution policy
decisions.recommended: Record actual Authenticode status and resolve signing/trusted distribution through the normal policy. Never bypass Windows protection prompts.
decisions.tradeoff: The retained installers are unsigned. Availability of a certificate and signing pipeline can affect the acceptance window.

decisions.title: Safe game and dedicated acceptance window
decisions.recommended: Approve exact installer/mod hashes and test targets at action time; use copied saves and disposable profiles for fault/uninstall cases, with one real authorized dedicated path.
decisions.tradeoff: A unavailable game/server leaves a real acceptance gap. A development snapshot cannot substitute for that path.

decisions.title: Residual issue policy
decisions.recommended: No waiver for P1 or known trust/data-loss/auth bypass issues. Lower-impact residuals require explicit scope, owner, workaround, expiry and approval.
decisions.tradeoff: A private tester release can document bounded low-impact limitations, but cannot be described as fully accepted when a mandatory environment test is blocked.

contracts.title: Identity precedes asynchronous work
contracts.rule: Capture the complete effective context before awaiting. Every completion validates context and epoch again before any store, cache, notification or file commit.
contracts.example: A starts loading; B becomes selected; A finishes late. A is discarded rather than ingested under B's label.

contracts.title: Newer has a defined ordering domain
contracts.rule: Compare source revisions only within their source epoch/context. Local request sequences serialize legacy same-context work but do not pretend to be cross-source production timestamps.
contracts.example: Epoch E2/revision 1 can supersede epoch E1/revision 500 through an explicit epoch transition.

contracts.title: Production time is not receipt time
contracts.rule: Persist source production metadata separately from local received/validated time and game elapsed time. Rereading unchanged bytes does not establish new production.
contracts.example: An unstamped export reopened tomorrow is still source-age unknown, not produced today.

contracts.title: Empty, omitted, failed and disabled differ
contracts.rule: Authoritative successful empty clears data. Omitted/failed sections retain last-known-good only with truthful degradation. Disabled follows an explicit visibility/retention policy.
contracts.example: A sold herd stays empty after restart; an exception does not falsely sell the herd.

contracts.title: Clear survives persistence
contracts.rule: A context/generation-scoped clear removes or invalidates matching derived detail and persists across restart. Older snapshots cannot resurrect it.
contracts.example: Zero-head summary plus a retained two-animal detail file yields zero current animals.

contracts.title: Measured zero is meaningful
contracts.rule: Finite zero is preserved through sample aggregation, normalization, formatting and warnings. Missing/nonfinite values remain unknown or explicitly estimated.
contracts.example: An all-zero health sample displays 0%, not 100% and not silently absent.

contracts.title: Population estimates do not rewrite sample means
contracts.rule: Keep observed sample size/mean distinct from reconciled population counts; adjust compatible sums only under a documented statistical rule.
contracts.example: Scaling a bucket from 3 sampled animals to 30 estimated animals cannot divide the original sum by 30.

contracts.title: Entity matching is one-to-one
contracts.rule: All matching indices share canonical consumed identity; ownership requires an authoritative source and field/farmland namespaces remain distinct.
contracts.example: A vehicle matched by configuration is unavailable for a second UID match.

contracts.title: Success follows committed bytes
contracts.rule: Validate staged content, preserve recoverable last-good data and advance freshness/dirty bookkeeping only after supported commit postconditions are met.
contracts.example: EACCES during replacement leaves the old final available and the operation failed.

contracts.title: Invalid origin is never native absence
contracts.rule: Missing, opaque, malformed and valid Origin are separate states. Origin, authentication, proxy policy and IPC sender identity are independently enforced.
contracts.example: Origin:null from a browser cannot inherit the native no-Origin loopback path.

contracts.title: Target ownership governs writes
contracts.rule: Multiple editions may read one save, but one authorized writer owns each actual game/remote target. Profile separation and a responding peer port are not sufficient.
contracts.example: RF in read-only mode explains why Classic currently owns game-facing settings writes.

contracts.title: Every expensive path is bounded
contracts.rule: Budget examined entries, elapsed time, in-flight operations, total network duration and eventual progress. Cancellation must reach the commit boundary.
contracts.example: A million rejected non-bales cannot be scanned in one slice simply because zero bales were accepted.

contracts.title: Unknown settings cannot overwrite known state
contracts.rule: Load state, draft, validation, revision and per-section commit outcomes are explicit. All requested validation precedes writes.
contracts.example: A failed Settings load never saves default values over an existing configuration.

contracts.title: Evidence names the layer and exact build
contracts.rule: Implemented, verified in workspace, packaged, installed and live/dedicated accepted are separate states. Each promotion requires its own evidence.
contracts.example: A correct development pasture screenshot cannot close installed Classic/RF coexistence.

performance.proposal: Establish before/after startup and section-action budgets on one reference machine and frozen dataset; approve a numeric threshold before optimizing.

performance.gate: No unexplained sustained growth or loss of progress; report duration and limitations rather than claiming leak-free forever.

runbooks.title: Unsafe write, cache escape or last-good loss
runbooks.trigger: Unexpected outside write, deleted valid final, exporter false success or repeated commit failure.
steps: Stop the affected writer/poller; keep the UI read-only or explicitly stale.
Preserve final/tmp/backup/journal files and redacted logs in the test environment.
Record exact build, context and operation phase; do not repeatedly retry against potentially damaged state.
Recover through the documented last-good protocol and a compatible known-good private build.
Reopen RP-03/04/05/06 as appropriate and rerun its cross-layer and installed acceptance before re-enabling writes.

runbooks.trigger: A payload appears under the wrong context, a legitimate clear reverses or an older revision replaces a newer one.
steps: Stop automatic ingestion for the affected context and display unavailable/stale rather than mislabeling it.
Capture context/epoch/revision/request sequence and frozen source payloads with secrets removed.
Preserve persisted evidence; invalidate only derived caches after capturing the reproduction.
Fix the owning ingestion/provenance path and rerun switch, restart and clear cases together.
Do not close the issue from a later correct screenshot; demonstrate the original ordering sequence now passes.

runbooks.title: Auth, IPC or proxy boundary regression
runbooks.trigger: Protected bootstrap without authorization, an untrusted sender accepted or credentials exposed in logs/UI.
steps: Disable the affected exposure or withdraw the candidate; do not widen trust for compatibility.
Preserve redacted denial/operation evidence without copying secrets into the audit repository.
Determine exact reachable route/frame/document and revoke affected test credentials if required through the approved owner.
Repair policy and exercise the full route/bridge matrix, not only the observed handler.
Resume only after security owner review and exact packaged/installed proof.

runbooks.title: Installer, migration or uninstall defect
runbooks.trigger: Other-edition data, browser preferences, shared game files or unknown paths are changed unexpectedly.
steps: Stop destructive testing immediately and preserve the disposable profile/VM state.
Record resolved target paths, ownership decisions and installer/hash identity.
Restore only the pre-recorded test snapshot after diagnosis; never guess the user's active-profile restore target.
Narrow cleanup/migration behavior and add the exact sentinel regression.
Repeat Keep, Full, upgrade and coexistence cases on a fresh disposable profile.

runbooks.title: Mod rollback during game acceptance

steps: Pause testing and close the game safely before changing a loaded mod.
Preserve the game log and exact candidate ZIP hash; record save/map/mod set and generation.
Restore the agreed compatible test mod/profile/save combination, not an arbitrary older ZIP.
Reproduce with supported local API references and isolated fixtures before another live attempt.
Repeat actual engine and dedicated acceptance for the corrected uniquely identified candidate.

runbooks.title: Private artifact withdrawal

steps: Identify the affected immutable build and stop further approved distribution.
Tell the approved tester group which exact build to stop using and provide safe rollback instructions.
Preserve the bad packet and reports for diagnosis; do not replace bytes in place.
Build a distinct corrected private candidate and rerun affected source, packaging and installed gates.
Keep public 4.2.1 assets and story unchanged throughout the incident.

steps.text: Define a context identity from configured source/server, save identity, farm scope and source epoch using fields actually available in the application and game. Document any fallback whose uniqueness is weaker than a durable save ID.
Define a monotonic source revision within an epoch and a local request sequence within a selected context. Never sort opaque UUIDs or compare unrelated wall clocks to establish payload ordering.

Specify how legacy unstamped exports are handled. Persist original observation metadata and display unknown or limited-confidence age; a reread or restart must not silently create a new source production time.
Separate producedAt, receivedAt, lastValidatedAt and displayed age. Record units and clock domains explicitly; game elapsed seconds are not UTC timestamps.
Specify section outcomes as successful data, authoritative empty, omitted, failed or disabled. These names are proposed contract labels, not claims about fields already present in the product.

Specify generation-scoped clear/tombstone semantics. A successful empty section clears current and persisted detail; a failed or omitted section may retain last-known-good data only with visible stale/unknown status.

Define detail provenance: context, pen identity, summary generation, detail generation and authoritative count. Define compatibility and bounded refresh behavior when a legacy producer cannot supply each field.

Define a structured error taxonomy separating authentication rejection, authorization failure, path missing, permission denied, transport outage, timeout, cancellation, malformed data and partial persistence.

Define write success as validated committed bytes plus truthful completion metadata. Define cancellation and stale-generation behavior immediately before commit, crash recovery and whether multiple files can be committed transactionally.
Document additive schema rollout and old/new compatibility. Readers tolerate explicitly supported old schemas; writers avoid silently changing meaning under existing field names.
Agree proposed acceptance thresholds, writer ownership and auth policy before implementation. Record the rationale and the consuming modules so later fixes do not diverge into local heuristics.

steps.text: Inventory sensitive HTTP routes, WebSocket upgrade paths and every privileged IPC handler exposed by preload. Record required capability, allowed caller and side effects for each; include reads that disclose configuration.

Represent a missing Origin, the literal opaque origin null, malformed values and a valid origin as distinct parse results. Never collapse an invalid browser origin into the no-Origin native-client path.
Enforce explicit accepted origin rules for browser HTTP and WebSocket traffic. Keep origin validation separate from authentication; CORS headers alone are not write authorization.
Define the no-Origin client policy per route. Privileged writes require the approved app-session/admin capability or an explicitly documented narrow exception, not merely a loopback network address.
Tie desktop IPC authorization to the expected BrowserWindow/webContents, main frame and exact trusted loaded document. Apply the guard before validation or side effects on every privileged handler.

Replace basename-only index.html/setup.html trust with canonical packaged paths. For development, allow only the explicitly configured scheme, host and effective port, never an omitted port treated as the application port.
Unify navigation, redirect and new-window policy with the IPC document policy. Route approved external URLs through the intended external opener without making them trusted privileged documents.
Define proxy behavior explicitly. Unless a deployment is configured and tested for proxy trust, do not treat rewritten localhost Host or forwarding headers as proof of a privileged local caller.
Add redacted denial diagnostics that identify the boundary and reason without logging tokens or credentials. Return structured errors that the UI can recover from.

Exercise all entry points with synthetic senders and a local test server, then test actual Electron navigation/frame boundaries in a disposable profile. Preserve the distinction between a permissive helper and proven hostile-document reachability.

packages.title: Preserve last-good desktop data through failed replacement
packages.outcome: Make desktop cache replacement recoverable on write, rename, cancellation and process-crash failures.
packages.status: Planned; reproduce against current production code before editing

steps.text: Identify every desktop download-to-final path, including both FTP XML and animal detail. Route them through one production commit abstraction rather than fixing only the reproduced branch.

Define the supported Windows replacement operation and recovery protocol. Confirm overwrite/rename behavior with actual filesystem tests during implementation; do not assume POSIX atomic replacement semantics.

Stage into a unique same-directory temporary file with restrictive appropriate access. Check context cancellation and destination ownership before starting and immediately before the irreversible commit step.
Complete and validate the staged payload before replacing the final file. Apply the relevant size, parse/schema and expected-source checks; do not declare a truncated JSON/XML transfer fresh.
Never unlink the last-good destination merely to make rename succeed. Use a tested replacement/backup protocol that preserves a recoverable last-good copy until committed bytes are confirmed.
Bound retry/backoff for sharing violations and permission errors. Surface a degraded/stale state when replacement fails instead of looping forever or announcing fresh data.

If the chosen Windows protocol has multiple steps, record enough recovery state to distinguish staged, backed-up and committed states after a crash. Keep recovery files contained and associated with the exact context.
Advance cache generation and freshness metadata only after successful commit. A canceled old poll must not publish a file or metadata after a new source configuration is active.

Implement startup recovery for each interrupted state and a bounded cleanup policy for obsolete temporary files. Never delete ambiguous recovery data until a valid final or recoverable last-good file is identified.
Keep the prior retained diagnostic as a historical counterexample; add real temporary-filesystem and injected-failure tests against the production commit abstraction.

Cross-file transactions may not be available; represent partial outcomes rather than claiming atomicity.
rollback: Stop new transfers before rollback. Preserve final, staged, backup and journal files until their generations are reconciled.

packages.title: Make mod persistence and collector outcomes truthful
packages.outcome: Stop reporting successful exports or empty successful collections when the underlying game operation failed.
packages.status: Planned; reproduce against current production code before editing

steps.text: Consult the local FS25 wiki, extracted scripts, LUADOC and examples for every copy, move, write, close and saveFile operation used by the exporter. Record exact signatures and return conventions before changing checks.
Create a persistence result adapter that distinguishes thrown errors, documented failure returns and successful completion. A nonthrowing pcall alone is not proof of a successful write.
Propagate copy/move results instead of discarding them. Never delete the source temporary file merely because a destination already exists from an older generation.

Check write and close outcomes according to the actual API contract. Where an API has no reliable success return, use a supported verification or explicitly report uncertainty/failure rather than inventing a boolean convention.
Unify normal, fallback, direct, atomic and mirror export paths under the same postconditions. Remove unsafe in-place fallback behavior that can damage the last-good export while reporting success.
Advance exported-generation markers, dirty-state clearing and success timestamps only after the correct payload is committed. Preserve retryable dirty work on failure.

Represent collector failure, successful empty data, omitted sections and disabled collectors distinctly. Catch failures at a boundary that preserves useful diagnostics without relabeling them as empty success.

Allow healthy sections to progress only under the agreed section-level contract; display stale retained sections honestly. Avoid an all-or-nothing policy that silently starves otherwise valid updates.

Trace all request polling and detail-rotation paths. Inject sustained collector failure to determine whether freshness-gated cycle tails are the only servicing path; if so, move servicing to an independent bounded cadence.
Add deterministic adapter-level fault cases, then schedule real game validation against a copied test save. Do not fault-inject disk operations against the user's active Save 1.
Validate both Classic and RF mod packaging against the corrected shared source and edition-specific configuration. A correction in one ZIP does not prove the other ZIP contains it.

packages.title: Make bootstrap, refresh and save selection context-safe
packages.outcome: Keep the selected save and displayed data aligned across startup, late responses, setup round-trips and restarts.
packages.status: Planned; reproduce against current production code before editing

steps.text: Reproduce the two prior response-order races and discovery failure before modifying current code. If a current fix already works, add production-linked proof and retain it.

Capture configured source identity, save/farm context, context epoch and request sequence before every asynchronous request. Apply this to initial bootstrap as well as manual refresh and fallback polling.

Centralize ingestion so HTTP, WebSocket, cache hydration and reconnect cannot bypass the same context/revision checks. Reject obsolete completions before they update the store, notifications or derived caches.
Cancel obsolete requests on context change but retain post-await guards because cancellation is not guaranteed to prevent a late completion.

Order same-context payloads by the agreed source revision; where supported legacy data lacks a revision, use documented serialization/coalescing rules rather than treating completion order as freshness.
Persist the selected stable source/save identifier only when selection is valid. Do not use a visible label or array position as durable identity.

On startup or return from setup, restore the last selected available context, otherwise explain the fallback and select a valid configured context. Handle a removed save without showing another save's data beneath its label.

Distinguish successful discovery of zero configured servers from failed discovery. Handle status before body parsing and give 401/403, 503, malformed JSON and transport failure different recovery states.
Retry the full discovery/bootstrap sequence when appropriate so a 503 followed by 200 rebuilds the selector without a page reload. Bound retry with backoff and user-visible retry controls.
Keep old data visible only if clearly labeled as the previous or stale context during a transition; do not render it as fresh data for the newly selected save.
Add actual Preact/store integration cases covering splash dismissal, setup return, restart restoration and interleaved WS/HTTP delivery.

packages.outcome: Keep generation and source age intact from export to disk cache, merge, restart and detail response.
packages.status: Planned; reproduce against current production code before editing

steps.text: Carry the RP-02 context, source epoch and generation metadata through cache envelopes and detail hydration instead of dropping generatedAt or its documented successor.

Separate remote/source freshness from local file receipt mtime. Persist original source and first-observed metadata so downloading or restarting cannot make unchanged stale data appear newly produced.
Define a bounded detail revalidation policy when a dirty index is missing or incomplete. Do not treat absence of the index as proof that every retained detail file is current forever.
Reject or refresh detail whose context/summary generation is incompatible. A successful authoritative zero pen must invalidate its old animal detail even when a disk cache still contains rows.
Replace generic empty-object hold logic with section outcome rules. Persist generation-scoped clears/tombstones so a legitimate clear survives process restart and snapshot restoration.
Preserve last-known-good data on failed or omitted collection only with an explicit degraded state. Avoid both silent resurrection and destructive clearing on transient failure.

Replace max-mtime plus total-size XML identity with a deterministic per-file identity covering the relevant paths. Decide whether content hashes are required for equal-size/equal-mtime changes and document the cost/guarantee.
Include every relevant section, including weather, in content-change detection or use a complete producer revision. Do not let an unchanged unrelated section suppress weather-only updates.
Migrate old persisted cache records conservatively. Missing provenance yields unknown/legacy confidence and bounded refresh, not manufactured current timestamps.
Use the RP-05 commit result as the only trigger to publish updated cache metadata. Prevent stale poller completions from writing new freshness records.
Test source restart, application restart, pen removal/recreation, network interruption and generation rollover together, not only a single read in memory.

An old reader may not understand new tombstones; rollout and rollback must account for schema compatibility.

steps.text: Reproduce the new hook's same-context new-generation case and A-to-B same-pen-ID case using actual Preact effects. Do not rely on the retained simulated hook scheduler as the final proof.
Key detail cache/in-flight work by complete context and relevant generation, not only pen ID. Reset or partition refs synchronously with the effective context used by the hydration effect.
Ensure an unchanged pen ID with a new summary generation can refresh its detail. Separate request deduplication from permanent already-hydrated suppression.
Guard every asynchronous completion with the captured context and generation. Abort obsolete work and prevent old responses from updating new-context state even when cancellation races.
Treat finite authoritative zero count as a valid target, distinct from missing/nonfinite totals. Reconcile cluster counts to targets 0, 1, 5 and larger without retaining hidden nonzero rows.

Use one in-flight verification operation per auth context and deduplicate submit/Enter/click races. Give network verification a bounded deadline without turning elapsed time into authorization.

Verify application/profile/session identifiers, shortcuts, installer identities, update channels and launch arguments together. A different port alone does not establish edition isolation.

Define writer transfer, process crash, stale ownership and unknown ownership behavior. Default uncertain ownership to read-only with a clear explanation rather than racing a write.

steps.text: At execution time obtain explicit approval for the exact installer hashes, target profile and game/mod switching window. The plan itself does not install, uninstall, replace a mod or authorize a live save change.

Record game version, map, mod set, save/farm identity, source generation and log timestamps. Compare installed dashboard summaries and detail against the same live or frozen generation.

Exercise animal zero/unknown cases, detail refresh, legitimate clears, reconnect and stale indicators through controlled test fixtures or copied-save scenarios, not destructive edits to the user's farm.

Run one real supported dedicated connection end to end: authenticated setup, initial XML/detail read, source update, detail change, disconnect/reconnect and transport-policy behavior. Record whether the path is FTP/FTPS or HTTP/HTTPS; do not claim untested protocols passed.

Run the agreed large-save and dedicated soak with measured poll overlap, request service delay, slice timing, memory and recovery. Use provisional durations from the plan only after confirming server availability and safe load.
Run Keep/Full uninstall and upgrade/migration sentinel tests only in disposable profiles. Confirm the other edition and shared game data survive before accepting uninstall ownership.
Collect screenshots, redacted logs, timestamps, exact artifact hashes and step outcomes. Restore only test-owned state after closing applications and record what was restored.

steps.text: Review the closure ledger with owners. Every P1, including the two previously unverified P1 cases, must have explicit closure evidence; known trust/data-loss defects are not waived into a tester build.

Require closure of release-critical P2 data, auth, transport, migration and packaging cases. Any lower-impact residual issue needs a named owner, bounded user impact, workaround, expiry and explicit product approval.
Verify all required installed/live/dedicated gates are passed. If an environment is unavailable, label the build unaccepted for that path and do not represent the whole plan as complete.
Prepare a concise tester README naming Classic/RF/mod pairings, unique private build ID, hashes, signature status, supported environment and installation prerequisites.

Give testers a numbered journey: install approved pair, load an agreed save, walk setup, select/restart a save, inspect overview/pasture/detail, exercise the approved dedicated path and report recovery behavior.

Provide an issue template requiring build ID/hash, edition, game/mod versions, context, source generation/time, reproduction steps, expected/actual result and redacted logs/screenshots. Explicitly exclude passwords and access codes.

Define stop-test triggers for save corruption, unexpected file deletion, cross-save data, unauthorized writes, credential exposure and repeated exporter failure. Tell testers to stop writes and preserve evidence, not retry destructively.
Keep distribution private and approved. Do not upload, publish, update public feeds or replace the Classic 4.2.1 public narrative as part of this handoff.
Set a human-owned triage process with severity, owner, reproduction and next candidate identity. This plan does not create an automation or promise unattended monitoring.
Document withdrawal and rollback instructions for the exact paired build. A corrected candidate receives a new immutable identity and targeted rerun of affected acceptance gates.
Obtain final sign-off on the private tester packet, not a blanket public release approval. Public release/versioning is a separate later decision.
